title: Reliability North Star orientation kit — Q4 2026
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a compact orientation kit for new reliability-facing stakeholders (product managers, platform owners, and eng teams) to align on a single reliability north star and a coordinated SLO adoption sprint for Q4 2026. The goal is alignment + a small set of reproducible experiments that make SLO ownership visible and low-friction to adopt.

Why this exists (short):
- Many teams ask: what SLOs should we target and how do we start without heavy process overhead?
- We want a minimal, repeatable onramp that scales to new services and to Dedicated/Private model-serving variants.
- Emphasize outcomes (customer-facing latency, request success, quality degradation) rather than infrastructure metrics only.

North Star statement (proposal):
"Customers experience consistent, predictable inference quality and latency across products: 99.9% of requests meet the service's configured latency SLO and quality acceptance checks, with clearly scoped fallbacks when degraded."

Orientation quick wins (first 2 weeks):
- Telemetry sanity check (owner: Jonah) — confirm logs, traces, and basic token-level latency visibility for top-10 routes. (JIRA REL-142)
- Error budget dashboard (owner: Asha) — create a shared dashboard that shows SLI -> SLO mapping and 30-day burn rate for pilot services.
- Smoke & canary checklist (owner: Miguel) — produce a 10-step smoke test that runs post-deploy and before incremental rollout.

Scope of the Q4 sprint (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): stakeholder kick, define service list (3 pilot services: hosted-text-gen, embeddings-indexer, reranker), map owners, runbook stub.
- Week 1–2: SLI definition & light instrumentation — agree on user-visible SLIs (p95 latency, success rate, semantic-quality baseline for reranker), implement lightweight collectors where missing.
- Week 3: Calibration & alerting — set provisional SLOs and configure alert thresholds for error-budget burn and latency regressions (pager + slack bridge).
- Week 4: Experimentation — run 2 induced-failure experiments (traffic spike, degraded model variant) to validate runbooks and fallbacks.
- Week 5: Rollout / Handoff — produce handoff notes, finalize runbooks, and schedule follow-up retro.

Example SLIs (recommended for pilot services):
- Hosted-text-gen: request_success_rate (200 OK and no model error) over 1 minute; latency_p95 for generation <= 350ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens).
- Embeddings-indexer: ingestion_success_rate and batch_processing_lag_p99 <= 5s.
- Reranker: semantic-pass_rate measured vs canary reference set (automated eval) >= 95%.

Acceptance criteria for SLO adoption (per service):
- SLI data populated back 14 days (no large gaps).
- Dashboard tile shows SLO, current error budget, and one historical incident mapped to burn.
- Postmortem template linked and an escalation owner named.
- Minimum one automatic alert configured for >20% burn in 24h and for p95 latency breach.

Cross-functional roles and responsibilities (light):
- Service Owner (Product/Feature PM): defines customer impact and drives SLO targets.
- Infra/SRE owner: responsible for instrumentation, dashboards, and alert plumbing.
- Platform/Serving Runtime: provides guidance on achievable latency floors for model families and recommended fallbacks.
- Solutions Eng / CS: validates customer impact scenarios and helps with runbooks for enterprise tenants.

Communication & cadence:
- Weekly 30m sync (Wed 10:00) for pilot teams — status, blockers, and decisions.
- Bi-weekly show-and-tell: short demo of dashboards and incident simulations for GTM stakeholders.
- Slack channel: #rel-north-star — used for day-to-day questions and burn alerts.

Risk register (top items):
- Telemetry gaps: missing traces or uneven sampling — mitigation: fallback to synthetic tests and temporary blackbox probes.
- Overly aggressive SLOs: cause noisy paging — mitigation: provisional SLOs with 30-day calibration period; reduce noise with grouped alerts and burn-based routing.
- Model-quality drift: harder to detect with only latency/success — mitigation: add small automated evals as SLI for rerankers and generators when feasible.

Runbook sketch (one-liner steps):
1) Detect: alert triggers on error budget burn or p95 breach.
2) Triage: owner reviews recent deploys, infra events, and model-change PRs (link to PRs).
3) Contain: if burn > 50% in 6h, route traffic to a compatible lower-latency variant or enable cache layer.
4) Remediate: roll back or fix model variant; re-run smoke tests.
5) Communicate: post incident note to #prod-ops and tag affected customers.

Metrics & measurement plan (how we'll judge success):
- Adoption: number of services with live SLO dashboard (target: 6 by EOY).
- Visibility: mean time to detect (MTTD) for pilot incidents reduced by 40% in 90 days.
- Stability: average error budget burn across pilots < 10% per month after calibration.

Templates and artifacts to attach (TODO):
- SLI definition template (single page) — path: confluence/SLI-template
- Runbook template — path: confluence/Runbook-Stub
- Smoke test script examples (k6 + curl) — github:serving-runtime/tests/smoke/
- Example automated eval harness for reranker — github:evals/rerank-ref

Open questions / items for decision (needs PM + Eng leadership):
- Should quality-eval SLIs be mandatory for any reranker/model-serving SLO?
- Which teams are on-call for model-quality regressions (platform or product)?
- Tiering: do we enforce different SLO targets for hosted vs dedicated vs private? Proposed: hosted = stricter, private = configurable.

Next actions (this doc owner: Evelyn):
- Send kickoff invite with attached agenda and the three pilot services (by 2026-10-18).
- Create initial dashboard skeleton and share credentials with pilot owners (by 2026-10-22).
- Open a short-lived cross-team epic in Jira to track the work (REL-2026 sprint).

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep the first sprint deliberately small — shipping visibility beats perfect instrumentation.
- Reuse existing synthetic load tests from infra-team rather than building new ones.
- Consider bundling a tiny "SLO starter kit" package for new services that automates dashboards and alerts via IaC.

Appendix: example short sprint checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Stakeholder kickoff held and service list confirmed
- [ ] Owner mapped for each role (PM, SRE, Platform)
- [ ] SLIs chosen and collectors instrumented (p95 latency, success_rate, semantic_eval)
- [ ] Dashboard with error budget visible
- [ ] At least one alert configured for budget burn
- [ ] Smoke test runnable from CI or k8s job
- [ ] Runbook stub in Confluence linked in dashboard
- [ ] Retro scheduled and 90-day follow-up milestone set

End of kit — for feedback add notes directly to this doc or ping me in Slack.
